title: Robot Material Alchemist Workshop
description: A robot stands at a workshop table between an iridescent lamp and a glass hurricane candle holder. The user commands the robot to extract material properties (iridescence, transparency, roughness, metalness, emissive color, refraction) from one object and transfer them onto the other, mixing and layering effects while respecting a total 'material energy' conservation budget. Full undo/redo support lets the user experiment freely.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load IridescenceLamp.glb on the left, GlassHurricaneCandleHolder.glb on the right, and robot.glb in the center on a dark metallic circular platform. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,6) looking at origin, with ambient light (0.3), a warm point light inside the lamp area, and a cool directional light from above. Use an EquirectangularReflectionMapping environment via PMREMGenerator with a generated neutral HDR for reflections.

Implement a material property system with six channels: iridescence intensity (0-1), transmission/transparency (0-1), roughness (0-1), metalness (0-1), emissive intensity (0-1), and ior/refraction (1.0-2.5). Each object starts with canonical values (lamp: high iridescence/emissive; candle holder: high transmission/low roughness). Define a conservation law: total material energy across both objects is fixed at the sum of their initial weighted channel values. Transferring a property increase to one object must decrease it proportionally on the other.

Create an HTML panel with: (1) source selector (lamp or holder), (2) six sliders for each channel, (3) a 'Transfer' button that triggers the robot to animate (rotate toward source, extend arm, glow, rotate toward target, apply), (4) an energy budget bar showing remaining allocation, (5) undo and redo buttons maintaining a history stack of up to 20 states. Each transfer counts as one interaction step. Sliders are coupled: adjusting one slider auto-constrains others to maintain conservation. Apply MeshPhysicalMaterial on both objects, updating iridescence, transmission, roughness, metalness, emissiveIntensity, and ior in real time after each robot transfer animation. The robot should visually glow with the transferred property color during animation using emissive on its meshes. Ensure at least 10-14 meaningful steps are needed to fully remix both objects' appearances. Add a 'Reset All' button that animates the robot returning properties to defaults.
